subject: Discovery recap & evaluation playbook — next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Leah Rogers <leah.rogers@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & evaluation playbook — next steps

Leah — thanks again for the 30-min call earlier. Quick recap (so we’re aligned) and a proposed playbook for the competitive evaluation you requested. I included Laura (solutions) and Monica (account ops) to scope the test matrix and logistics.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Unreliable tail latency from current cloud endpoints (spikes > 500ms on p95 for 1–2k token prompts).
- Cost unpredictability at scale — current monthly spend on embeddings+generation is creeping up and you need better cost models.
- Inconsistent labels/outputs when running ensemble models across different vendors (model drift in production).

Current stack (from call):
- Inference: TGI (self-managed) for experimental workloads, cloud managed endpoints (vendor X) for prod features.
- Orchestration: internal service layered on AWS ECS + S3 storage for prompts/data.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 in-scope, strict data retention policies; no PHI.

Success criteria you called out (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for single-turn prompts up to ~512 tokens; p95 < 400ms for generative flows ~1–2k tokens.
- Quality: generation accuracy on your labeled validation set (F1 / custom metric) to be within 3% of baseline.
- Cost: predictable unit cost with target effective cost < $0.60 per 1k generated tokens (target to beat current by at least 20%).
- Operational: ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant during capacity events.

Proposed evaluation scope (high level):
- Endpoints to benchmark: Redwood hosted API (Prod), Redwood Dedicated (AWS rtx class), vLLM self-hosted (your cluster), TGI baseline (your current).
- Workloads: 1) short-query Q&A (<=128 tokens), 2) mid-length completions (512 tokens), 3) long generative flows (1–2k tokens) using your sample prompts.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, mean tokens/sec throughput, per-1k token cost, output quality (your labeled testset), memory/KV cache behavior.
- Duration: 72-hour comparative run per endpoint to capture variance; peak-hour synthetic bursts included.

Attachments: redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (playbook + run matrix) and sample-benchmark-sheets.xlsx (template for results).

Next steps (proposal):
1) You confirm the success criteria and provide a small labeled validation set (10–1000 examples depending on tolerance) and a representative prompt corpus.
2) Grant temporary access to your eval sandbox (S3 path) or share a downloadable sample.
3) We schedule a 1-hour kickoff with Laura to finalize the matrix and timelines (I recommend starting the week of Oct 19).
4) Redwood will execute the comparative runs and deliver a concise report + recommended configuration (quantization, batching, routing policy).

If that looks right, please confirm and I’ll create a short mutual action plan (MVP + milestones + owner assignments).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood-eval-playbook.pdf (application/pdf), sample-benchmark-sheets.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Leah Rogers <leah.rogers@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Harper <ben.harper@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & evaluation playbook — next steps

Sergio — thanks for the tidy recap. All of that aligns with what we talked about. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Validation set: we can share ~1k labeled examples from last quarter (intent + expected completion) and a larger unlabeled corpus (10k prompts). I’ll attach a small sample (acme-eval-sample-queries.csv) here.
2) SOC2: SOC2 report & evidence requests will be required before we route any production data. Can you confirm Redwood’s SOC2 status and provide the latest report?
3) Sandbox: Ben will provision an S3 eval sandbox and a test IAM role (read-only for the sample data). We prefer the tests run against anonymized data only.

Acceptance criteria tweaks: we’re comfortable with p95 up to 250ms for short prompts if throughput is significantly better; cost target is flexible if quality improves. The most important is consistent tails and determinism during burst windows.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll share the labeled set and S3 details by COB Mon Oct 12.
- Ben will coordinate network access and compliance gating.

Thanks — excited to see the matrix.

—
Leah Rogers
Head of Product, Integrations
Acme Analytics
leah.rogers@acmeanalytics.com

Attachment: acme-eval-sample-queries.csv (text/csv)

Thanks Leah — perfect. Two quick items: 

1) SOC2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant (latest report: Q2 2026). I’ve linked the report in the playbook share and can route the auditor pack to your security team once you complete the NDA stage.
2) Data access: please send the S3 path + IAM role ARN when ready. For the initial run we’ll pull only the labeled set; please confirm the anonymization step (we do not need PII).

Proposed timeline:
- Mon Oct 12: Acme shares labeled set + S3 details.
- Wed Oct 14: 30-min kickoff with Laura to finalize matrix (Laura — are you available Wed 10/14 10:00–11:00 PT?).
- Oct 19–22: Redwood performs comparative runs (72-hour windows as proposed).
- Oct 26: Deliverable — results deck + recommended config.

I’ve pasted a short checklist below for Ben/Leah to confirm quickly: 
- [ ] Labeled validation set shared (S3 path)
- [ ] IAM role set up for redwood-infra-readonly
- [ ] SOC2 NDA path confirmed
- [ ] Priority endpoints to include (Redwood hosted, Redwood Dedicated on AWS, vLLM self-hosted, TGI baseline)

Laura/Monica — I’ll rely on you two to produce the benchmark matrix and run the jobs once we have the S3 access.

Best,
Sergio

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Leah Rogers <leah.rogers@acmeanalytics.com>, Ben Harper <ben.harper@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark matrix & execution questions — Acme eval

Hi all — looping in with a draft benchmark matrix (attached: redwood-benchmark-matrix.xlsx) and a few execution questions so we can lock the runbook during the Wed kickoff.

Draft matrix highlights (please flag changes):
- Endpoints: Redwood hosted API (region us-west-2), Dedicated (rtx-class pool on AWS us-west-2), vLLM (your self-hosted instance on m5/g4 mix), TGI (your current baseline).
- Models: we’ll test a comparable 7B variant and a 13B quantized variant where available to match your quality/cost targets.
- Load profile: steady-state at 50 concurrent requests + periodic spike to 300 RPS for 10 minutes to observe tail behavior.
- Quality evaluation: run labeled set through each endpoint, compute application F1 and a simple perplexity proxy when possible.
- Cost calc: include raw infra (hours * GPU price) + per-request infra overhead to compute effective per-1k-token cost.

Questions for Acme: 
1) Can you confirm which models you consider your current production baseline (name/version)?
2) Do you want us to include batching experiments (yes/no)? Batching can change latency/cost tradeoffs substantially.
3) Any additional acceptance criteria beyond latency/quality/cost (e.g., cold-start time, KV cache hit rate reporting)?

If Leah/Ben confirm the S3 path and IAM role today, we’ll finalize the matrix and bring an execution plan to the Wed meeting.

Thanks — Laura
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-benchmark-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
